does: Cooks onions slowly until their water is gone and their sugars turn deep brown, soft and sweet.
how: Sweat sliced onions in butter with a little salt until soft.
Take the lid off and keep the heat at medium-low.
Stir every little while, scraping up the brown film that forms on the bottom of the pan.
Add a spoonful of water whenever the film darkens faster than the onions.
Stop when they are the colour of dark honey all the way through.

cues.text: An even, deep amber, a fraction of the raw heap, with no black edges.
Sweet and nutty, like toast and caramel. A sharp, acrid smell means they are burning.
As sweet as jam, with no sharpness left.

mistakes.mistake: Rushing with high heat, which burns the edges and leaves the middle pale and bitter.
mistakes.fix: Keep the heat low and give it the time it takes. There is no shortcut.

mistakes.mistake: Crowding a small pan, so that the onions steam and never brown.
mistakes.fix: Use the widest pan you have.

comes_after.why: Onions sweat before they caramelize. The first stage is the same move.
